Not backed: (1) the trigger as worded, i.e. significant sleepiness despite an adequate opportunity to sleep (the NHS page addresses insomnia, and line 47 says constant daytime tiredness probably means not enough sleep); (2) the contrast 'zamiast jedynie zwiększać ilość kofeiny': neither snapshot says anything about using caffeine to counter sleepiness (NHS mentions caffeine only as a cause of insomnia and says to avoid tea or coffee at least 6 hours before bed). Searched both cited snapshots for caffeine, sleepiness, daytime tiredness and GP advice.

quotes.text: wake up several times during the night
still feel tired after waking up
Things that keep you from getting a good night's sleep:

claims.reason: No snapshot states in general terms that sleep quality matters in addition to duration. The NHS page lists fragmented sleep and feeling tired after waking among insomnia symptoms and lists conditions that keep you from a good night's sleep, which only indirectly supports the point. The Van Dongen abstract manipulates time in bed, not sleep quality. Searched both cited snapshots for quality, disturbed or fragmented sleep and tiredness.

claims.claim: Badanie nie określa dokładnej potrzeby każdej osoby
claims.reason: This is a claim of absence about the study. The Van Dongen snapshot is an abstract only, which cannot show absence; the full text would be needed to confirm that no individual sleep need was estimated. The abstract is consistent with it (fixed 4/6/8 h doses, group-level dose-response, population-level model) but does not state it.

claims.claim: nie uzasadnia samodzielnego leczenia zaburzeń snu

quotes.text: Check with your doctor before taking anything for your sleep problems.

scope_gaps.note: The study shows that self-rated sleepiness under-represented performance deficits in sleep-restricted healthy adults (21-38 y, laboratory, 14 days). It did not test people who report no sleepiness at all; a reader might assume that case was tested. Only the abstract was checked.
The NHS page addresses insomnia (trouble sleeping), not persistent sleepiness despite adequate opportunity to sleep. Nothing in either snapshot concerns caffeine as a response to sleepiness.
The 14 days apply to the restriction arms; the abstract gives total sleep deprivation as 3 nights without sleep. The sentence does not say otherwise but a reader might assume 14 days for both.

Deficits and the sleepiness comparison come from healthy adults aged 21-38 under laboratory restriction. The 'largely unaware' statement is the authors' interpretation ('suggest'), stated in the abstract's conclusions.

The abstract states randomisation only for the chronic sleep restriction experiment (4/6/8 h); how the total sleep deprivation experiment was allocated is not described. The plural 'badania' is two experiments in one paper. The NHS source is an insomnia information page whose 'How much sleep you need' section carries the general sleep-need figures.
Sleep quality as an additional factor is not stated generally in either snapshot; the NHS page only implies it through symptoms of insomnia.
Absence about what the study estimated cannot be shown from an abstract-only snapshot.
